stories.headline: Ukraine resumes drone strikes on Russian oil refineries
body: Ukraine has restarted attacks on Russian oil refineries, despite pressure from Donald Trump before the US midterms.
Russian state media said drones set fire to the Kstovo refinery, after a big strike on a Rosneft refinery in Samara.
The local ceasefire in occupied Oleshky ended on Sunday night.
stories.vc: Hits on Russian refineries tighten fuel supply and can push up diesel prices worldwide.

stories.headline: Gulf states 'braced for the worst' as Hormuz talks drag on
body: Indirect US–Iran talks in Doha went into a third day as Qatar tries to free more than $6 billion in Iranian assets.
That could lead to reopening the Strait of Hormuz and restarting nuclear talks.
Gulf officials are waiting for Washington's reply before Tuesday's US midterms.
stories.joke: Everyone's waiting on one reply. It's the world's most stressful group chat.
stories.vc: A Hormuz deal would cut oil and shipping costs fast; no deal keeps India's fuel import bill high.

stories.headline: Canada's Carney says US trade talks are making progress
body: Canadian PM Mark Carney said he had a good conversation with Trump about the future of Canada–US trade.
Both countries have hit each other with billions of dollars in tariffs in recent months.
The news came two days before the US midterm elections.
stories.joke: Two neighbours, one long call, and a lot of 'good conversation'.
stories.vc: A Canada–US deal would ease North American supply chains and lower costs for auto and metals firms.

stories.headline: Opposition rallies in Delhi over 130 million deleted voters
body: Thousands of opposition supporters rallied in Delhi as protests against the Modi government grow.
The Congress-led alliance is angry about a voter-roll revision that removed 130 million names.
Leaders say it helps the BJP and have called for the chief election commissioner to resign.
stories.vc: Political uncertainty around elections can make foreign investors cautious about Indian markets.

stories.headline: ED arrests Armstrong Exchange founder in betting scam probe
body: The Enforcement Directorate arrested Armstrong Exchange founder Sagar Dash over an alleged online gaming and betting scam.
It says mule accounts and shell firms moved hundreds of crores of illegal money.
About ₹9 crore was frozen and Edsom Fintech's CEO was also arrested.
stories.joke: Turns out the house always wins, until the ED shows up.
stories.vc: Crackdowns on betting-linked fintech raise compliance costs for payment startups that handle gaming money.

stories.headline: Work begins on Bengaluru's 250-metre skydeck
body: The Bangalore Development Authority has finalised land for a 250-metre skydeck and started work to invite designs.
The project, estimated at up to ₹500 crore, was approved by the Cabinet in August 2024.
Land prices around the site in Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layout may more than double, BDA sources say.
stories.joke: Bengaluru will finally have a place high enough to see the end of the traffic jam.
stories.vc: Landmark projects lift nearby land values, good for owners, harder for first-time buyers.

stories.headline: Binance restarts withdrawals after its $6.3B hack
body: Binance is letting users withdraw again, in phases, after hackers stole $6.3 billion.
It says it has covered 95% of the stolen assets and is buying the rest.
It promises users will not bear any losses.
stories.joke: Binance just ate a $6.3 billion loss and said 'we're fine'. Must be nice.
stories.vc: Covering losses in full protects trust, but shows how much capital big exchanges must hold for security failures.

stories.statLabel: when AI may be 'the issue', OpenAI says
stories.headline: OpenAI may rename data centres 'AI compute campuses'
body: Axios reports OpenAI is planning a PR push after Tuesday's midterms, as data centres grow unpopular.
Its global affairs chief Chris Lehane expects AI to be the big issue in the 2028 election.
Ideas include AI 'speed limits' and showing people how AI helps their daily lives.
stories.joke: Same buildings, nicer name. It worked for 'cloud'.
stories.vc: Public backlash is now a real cost for AI infrastructure; how labs manage it affects build-out timelines.

stories.statLabel: AV startups pitched to one VC this year
stories.headline: The self-driving startup boom is back, bigger than 2016
body: Trucks VC has seen pitches from 81 new autonomous vehicle startups so far in 2026.
Its partner says this year may be even hotter than the frothy 2016–17 deal days.
TechCrunch's mobility newsletter says a new, bigger AV boom is here.
stories.joke: Robotaxis: always five years away, now with more pitch decks.
stories.vc: Hot sectors attract crowded rounds and high prices; investors will need to pick winners carefully.

stories.statLabel: years since the last new fibre
stories.headline: Renoa: a startup's new fibre takes on cashmere
body: Startup Everbloom has made renoa, which TechCrunch calls the first new fibre in 25 years.
It aims to be a cheaper, easier-care alternative to cashmere.
Cashmere goats have been damaging rangelands across Central Asia.
stories.joke: Finally, softness without the goat guilt.
stories.vc: Materials startups are a quiet bet on luxury: Loro Piana's cashmere-heavy business is worth over €11 billion.

image.credit: Paul Esson from Bacchus Marsh, Australia / Wikimedia Commons

stories.statLabel: CEOs criticised for AI parenting tips
stories.headline: Are AI bosses too out of touch to build for normal people?
body: Marissa Mayer drew criticism for using AI to describe her daughter for a school task.
Sam Altman has suggested AI podcasts for kids' school runs; Mark Zuckerberg says AI may meet social needs.
TechCrunch asks whether AI leaders understand ordinary users.
stories.joke: Step 1: be a billionaire. Step 2: wonder why people don't love your parenting app.
stories.vc: Products built for executives often miss mass markets; consumer AI winners will be the ones that understand everyday life.

stories.headline: Bulgaria set to elect its first woman president
body: Acting President Iliana Iotova leads Bulgaria's presidential run-off with about 51%, exit polls show.
If confirmed on Monday, she will be the country's first elected female president.
Turnout was low at about 27–29%; the role is largely ceremonial.
stories.joke: A first for Bulgaria, decided by under a third of voters.
stories.vc: Women heads of state remain rare in Europe's east; each one shifts who gets seen as presidential.

stories.headline: Delhi women push to reclaim their right to enjoy nature
body: On a wildlife walk in Delhi, women shared stories of being harassed just for enjoying parks and forests.
Ecologist Vallari Sheel was shouted at for photographing a tree 50 metres from her home.
She tells female interns not to engage when men question them.
stories.vc: Safe public spaces decide whether women can work in fields like ecology at all.

stories.headline: Jacinda Ardern: rebuild trust through financial security
body: Former New Zealand PM Jacinda Ardern told a Sydney Opera House audience that politicians are making polarisation worse.
She urged leaders to avoid binary thinking and the language of violence.
She said trust can be rebuilt by giving people financial security.
stories.joke: Advice from the one politician people still quote kindly.
stories.vc: Economic insecurity fuels political anger; policies on wages and housing are now trust policies too.

image.credit: Office of the Clerk, NZ Parliament / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: KIMS doubles its Anantapur hospital to 500 beds
body: KIMS Hospitals expanded KIMS Saveera in Anantapur from 250 to 500 beds, taking the group to 9,117 beds.
The expansion adds a cancer block with a linear accelerator and PET-CT, plus a mother-and-child block with a neonatal ICU.
It was due to be formally opened on 1 November.
stories.joke: Twice the beds, and one less reason to travel to Hyderabad.
stories.vc: Regional chains growing in tier-2 cities like Anantapur are where much of India's new hospital capacity is coming from.

stories.headline: West Bengal seeks an AIIMS in Raiganj and a cancer hospital
body: West Bengal will ask the Centre to set up an AIIMS in Raiganj, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said.
The state also plans a full cancer hospital in Jalpaiguri.
An AIIMS in North Bengal was a BJP poll promise; the state's only AIIMS is in Kalyani.
stories.joke: North Bengal's long wait for an AIIMS may finally be getting a postcode.
stories.vc: A new AIIMS anchors medical colleges, jobs and private clinics around it for decades.

stories.headline: Telangana to offer free MRI scans in government hospitals
body: Telangana will add MRI services to government hospitals through a public–private partnership.
Mahbubnagar Government General Hospital will run the first pilot.
The health minister asked officials to plan a phased rollout.
stories.vc: PPP diagnostics let states add costly machines fast, a steady business for imaging companies.

stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh orders all government hospitals to upgrade ICUs
body: Government hospitals in Andhra Pradesh must upgrade their ICUs to national standards by set deadlines.
The order covers buildings, equipment, staff hiring and patient safety.
It follows Supreme Court directions from September on ICU guidelines.
stories.vc: Upgrading public ICUs creates demand for equipment makers and trained critical-care staff.

stories.headline: Haas drops Ocon for Mexico; he denies a physical row
body: Haas replaced Esteban Ocon with reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the rest of the Mexico City GP weekend.
It followed a radio dispute with his race engineer Laura Mueller over tyre choice in practice.
Ocon, who leaves Haas at season's end, denied a French report that a meeting with the team boss turned physical.
stories.joke: Asked for softs, got benched. Tyre arguments have consequences.
stories.vc: Driver-team blowups hurt sponsor value; Haas will want a calm line-up as it chases midfield points money.
